source_text: Aliud peccatum in sancta Domini, aliud in proximum. Utrumque altare tangit. Dilige Deum et proximum.
orientation: Origen is applying the Levitical sin-offering morally, distinguishing sins against God from sins against neighbor and tying both to the altar.
pass_a_gloss: One sin is against the holy things of the Lord, another against the neighbor. Each touches the altar. Love God and the neighbor.

choices.english: the holy things of the Lord
choices.why: Keeps the plural neuter 'sancta' as holy things, matching the Levitical context of sacred objects or offerings, not persons.
Preserves the present tense and the literal force of 'tangit' as touches, showing both kinds of sin have contact with the altar.
Keeps the imperative singular and the two objects as God and neighbor, echoing the double command.
rejected: You shall love God and neighbor

pass_b_english: One kind of sin is against the holy things of the Lord, another against the neighbor. Each touches the altar. Love God and the neighbor.
